quotes.text: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
quotes.speaker: Lao Tzu
quotes.note: Original: 千里之行，始於足下. English version is established translation but slightly simplified.

quotes.text: The only true wisdom is in knowing you know nothing.
quotes.speaker: Socrates
quotes.note: Socrates' actual position is more nuanced. This is the popular compression.

quotes.text: No wind serves him who addresses his voyage to no certain port.
quotes.speaker: Michel de Montaigne
quotes.note: Verified in Essays III.13.

quotes.text: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself—and you are the easiest person to fool.
quotes.speaker: Richard Feynman
quotes.note: Verified in recorded commencement address.

quotes.text: It is wrong always, everywhere, and for anyone, to believe anything upon insufficient evidence.
quotes.speaker: W. K. Clifford
quotes.note: Verified in published essay.

quotes.text: No man ever steps in the same river twice.
quotes.speaker: Heraclitus
quotes.note: Preserved through Plato and later authors. Exact wording varies.

quotes.text: Doubt is not a pleasant condition, but certainty is absurd.
quotes.speaker: Voltaire
quotes.note: Original French differs. This is the established English compression.

quotes.text: Perfection is achieved, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.
quotes.speaker: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
quotes.note: Verified in published work.

quotes.text: First, do no harm.
quotes.speaker: Hippocrates
quotes.note: The oath says 'I will abstain from all intentional wrong-doing and harm.' The exact phrase 'first do no harm' is a modern compression, possibly from Thomas Sydenham.

quotes.text: Act in such a way that you treat humanity, whether in your own person or in the person of any other, never merely as a means to an end, but always at the same time as an end.
quotes.speaker: Immanuel Kant
quotes.work: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
quotes.note: Verified in published work, Formula of Humanity.

quotes.text: Power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely.
quotes.speaker: Lord Acton
quotes.note: Verified in published correspondence.

quotes.text: Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.
quotes.speaker: Martin Luther King Jr.
quotes.note: Verified in published letter.

quotes.text: The sad truth is that most evil is done by people who never make up their minds to be good or evil.
quotes.speaker: Hannah Arendt
quotes.note: Arendt's actual formulation in Eichmann in Jerusalem is more complex. This is a popular compression.

quotes.text: An ounce of practice is worth more than tons of preaching.
quotes.speaker: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.note: Not reliably found in Gandhi's published works. May be a paraphrase.

quotes.text: Well done is better than well said.
quotes.speaker: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.note: Verified in published almanack.

quotes.text: Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it.
quotes.speaker: George Santayana
quotes.note: Verified in published work.

quotes.text: The struggle of man against power is the struggle of memory against forgetting.
quotes.speaker: Milan Kundera
quotes.work: The Book of Laughter and Forgetting
quotes.note: Verified in published novel.

quotes.text: You have power over your mind—not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
quotes.speaker: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.note: Compresses ideas from Meditations Book 6.8 and elsewhere. Not a direct quote.

quotes.text: Everything can be taken from a man but one thing: the last of the human freedoms—to choose one's attitude in any given set of circumstances, to choose one's own way.
quotes.speaker: Viktor Frankl
quotes.note: Verified in published work.

quotes.text: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
quotes.speaker: Aristotle
quotes.note: This is Will Durant's paraphrase from 'The Story of Philosophy' (1926), not Aristotle's words. Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics discusses habituation but in different terms.

quotes.text: Either mathematics is too big for the human mind, or the human mind is more than a machine.
quotes.speaker: Kurt Gödel
quotes.note: Reported in Hao Wang's 'From Mathematics to Philosophy' (1974). Not a direct published quote by Gödel.

quotes.text: Ikut resmi padi, makin berisi makin tunduk.
quotes.speaker: Peribahasa Melayu
quotes.note: Traditional proverb. The more grain, the more it bows.

quotes.text: Biar lambat, asal selamat.
quotes.speaker: Peribahasa Melayu
quotes.note: Better slow and safe.

quotes.text: Sedikit-sedikit, lama-lama jadi bukit.
quotes.speaker: Peribahasa Melayu
quotes.note: Little by little, it becomes a mountain.

quotes.text: Harimau mati meninggalkan belang, manusia mati meninggalkan nama.
quotes.speaker: Peribahasa Melayu
quotes.note: A tiger dies leaving its stripes, a person dies leaving their name.

quotes.text: Bagai aur dengan tebing.
quotes.speaker: Malay proverb
quotes.note: Like bamboo with the riverbank — mutual dependence.

quotes.text: Di mana bumi dipijak, di situ langit dijunjung.
quotes.speaker: Malay proverb
quotes.note: Where you stand on the earth, there you hold up the sky — respect local customs.

quotes.text: Sebab nila setitik, rosak susu sebelanga.
quotes.speaker: Malay proverb
quotes.note: One drop of indigo ruins a whole pot of milk.

quotes.text: Tak kenal maka tak cinta.
quotes.speaker: Malay proverb
quotes.note: Without knowing, there is no love.

quotes.text: Melentur buluh biarlah dari rebungnya.
quotes.speaker: Malay proverb
quotes.note: Bend the bamboo from the shoot — early education.

quotes.text: Berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing.
quotes.speaker: Malay proverb
quotes.note: Heavy loads carried together, light ones lifted together.

quotes.text: Tak ada rotan, akar pun berguna.
quotes.speaker: Malay proverb
quotes.note: No rattan? Roots will do — adaptability.

quotes.text: 知之為知之，不知為不知，是知也。
quotes.speaker: Confucius
quotes.note: To know what you know and know what you don't — that is knowledge.

quotes.text: 上善若水。水善利萬物而不爭。
quotes.speaker: Lao Tzu
quotes.note: The highest good is like water. Water benefits all things and does not compete.

quotes.text: 故兵貴勝，不貴久。
quotes.speaker: Sun Tzu
quotes.note: In war, value victory, not prolonged campaigns.

quotes.text: 君子和而不同。
quotes.speaker: Confucius
quotes.note: The gentleman is harmonious but not conformist.

quotes.text: 治大國，若烹小鮮。
quotes.speaker: Lao Tzu
quotes.note: Governing a great state is like cooking a small fish — don't overdo it.

quotes.text: 學而不思則罔，思而不學則殆。
quotes.speaker: Confucius
quotes.note: Learning without thought is labor lost; thought without learning is perilous.

quotes.text: 禍兮福之所倚，福兮禍之所伏。
quotes.speaker: Lao Tzu
quotes.note: Misfortune is what fortune depends upon; fortune is where misfortune hides.

quotes.text: 己所不欲，勿施於人。
quotes.speaker: Confucius
quotes.note: Do not impose on others what you do not wish for yourself.

quotes.text: The ink of the scholar is more sacred than the blood of the martyr.
quotes.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
quotes.note: Not found in the six major hadith collections (Bukhari, Muslim, etc.). May be a later fabrication or paraphrase.

quotes.text: He who knows himself knows his Lord.
quotes.speaker: Ibn Arabi
quotes.note: Attributed to Ibn Arabi and also to Prophet Muhammad in some traditions. Wording varies.

quotes.text: The cure for ignorance is to question.
quotes.speaker: Al-Ghazali
quotes.note: Accurately represents al-Ghazali's position on inquiry. Not a direct quote.

quotes.text: Waste no time debating what a good person should be. Be one.
quotes.speaker: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.note: Compresses ideas from Meditations. Not a direct quote.

quotes.text: He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.
quotes.speaker: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.display_label: Friedrich Nietzsche, quoted by Viktor Frankl (attribution uncertain)
quotes.note: This is Friedrich Nietzsche's quote (Twilight of the Idols, 1889). Frankl quoted Nietzsche in Man's Search for Meaning. The quote is Nietzsche's, not Frankl's.

quotes.text: The unexamined life is not worth living.
quotes.speaker: Socrates
quotes.note: Verified in Plato's Apology.

quotes.text: It is not death that a man should fear, but he should fear never beginning to live.
quotes.speaker: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.note: Compresses Meditations 12.1 and related passages. Not a direct quote.

quotes.text: What I cannot create, I do not understand.
quotes.speaker: Richard Feynman
quotes.note: Reported by those present at Feynman's death. Not in a published work.

quotes.text: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
quotes.speaker: Alan Turing
quotes.note: Verified in published paper.

quotes.text: The purpose of computing is insight, not numbers.
quotes.speaker: Richard Hamming
quotes.work: Numerical Methods for Scientists and Engineers
quotes.note: Verified in published work.

quotes.text: Premature optimization is the root of all evil.
quotes.speaker: Donald Knuth
quotes.work: Structured Programming with go to Statements
quotes.note: Verified in published paper.

quotes.text: Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.
quotes.speaker: Arthur C. Clarke
quotes.note: Clarke's Third Law. Verified in published work.

quotes.text: If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it well enough.
quotes.speaker: Albert Einstein
quotes.note: Not found in Einstein's published works or correspondence. Likely a modern fabrication.

quotes.text: In God we trust; all others bring data.
quotes.speaker: W. Edwards Deming
quotes.note: Not reliably sourced to Deming. The phrase predates him. May be a paraphrase of his emphasis on data.

quotes.text: The most exciting phrase to hear in science, the one that heralds new discoveries, is not 'Eureka!' but 'That's funny...'
quotes.speaker: Isaac Asimov
quotes.note: Widely attributed to Asimov. Exact source unclear.

quotes.text: As a person acts, so they become.
quotes.speaker: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad
quotes.note: Translation from Sanskrit. Wording varies by translator.

quotes.text: In the midst of winter, I found there was, within me, an invincible summer.
quotes.speaker: Albert Camus
quotes.note: Verified in published essay.

quotes.text: The greatest enemy of knowledge is not ignorance, it is the illusion of knowledge.
quotes.speaker: Stephen Hawking
quotes.note: Not reliably sourced to Hawking. Similar ideas appear in Daniel Boorstin's work.

quotes.text: Do not go where the path may lead, go instead where there is no path and leave a trail.
quotes.speaker: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.note: Emerson's actual words in 'Self-Reliance' differ. This is a popular compression.

quotes.text: The measure of intelligence is the ability to change.
quotes.speaker: Albert Einstein
quotes.note: Not found in Einstein's published works. Likely a modern fabrication.

quotes.text: Freedom is not worth having if it does not include the freedom to make mistakes.
quotes.speaker: Mahatma Gandhi
quotes.note: Not reliably sourced to Gandhi's published works.

quotes.text: I am because we are.
quotes.speaker: Ubuntu philosophy
quotes.note: Modern English formulation of Ubuntu philosophy. Not a direct translation of a specific text.

quotes.text: If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together.
quotes.speaker: African proverb
quotes.note: Widely attested across multiple African cultures.

quotes.text: The child who is not embraced by the village will burn it down to feel its warmth.
quotes.speaker: African proverb
quotes.note: Attribution to specific African culture varies. Widely circulated.

quotes.text: Wisdom is like a baobab tree; no one individual can embrace it.
quotes.speaker: African proverb
quotes.note: Akan origin, widely attested.

quotes.text: I have always believed that you must stand up for what you think is right, even if you are a voice of one.
quotes.speaker: Lee Kuan Yew
quotes.note: Consistent with Lee Kuan Yew's documented positions.

quotes.text: Bhinneka Tunggal Ika.
quotes.speaker: Mpu Tantular
quotes.note: Unity in diversity. From the Sutasoma poem, now Indonesian national motto.

quotes.text: A nation is not built in a day. It is built with patience, wisdom, and sacrifice.
quotes.speaker: Sukarno
quotes.note: Represents Sukarno's positions. Exact wording uncertain.

quotes.text: Nothing is more precious than independence and freedom.
quotes.speaker: Hồ Chí Minh
quotes.note: Verified in published declaration.

quotes.text: Man is condemned to be free.
quotes.speaker: Jean-Paul Sartre
quotes.note: Verified in published work.

quotes.text: The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
quotes.speaker: Ludwig Wittgenstein
quotes.note: Proposition 5.6. Verified in published work.

quotes.text: Hell is other people.
quotes.speaker: Jean-Paul Sartre
quotes.note: Spoken by the character Garcin in the play No Exit. Represents Sartre's philosophical position but is dramatic dialogue, not a philosophical proposition.

quotes.text: One cannot step twice into the same river.
quotes.speaker: Heraclitus
quotes.note: Duplicate of SENSE_Q_004. Preserved through later authors.

quotes.text: Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.
quotes.speaker: Immanuel Kant
quotes.work: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
quotes.note: Categorical Imperative. Verified in published work.

quotes.text: God is dead. God remains dead. And we have killed him.
quotes.speaker: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.note: Verified in published work. Often misunderstood out of context.

quotes.text: The life of man is solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Hobbes
quotes.note: Verified in published work.

quotes.text: No man is free who is not master of himself.
quotes.speaker: Epictetus
quotes.note: Represents Epictetus' position on self-mastery. Exact wording varies.

quotes.text: Nature, to be commanded, must be obeyed.
quotes.speaker: Bacon

quotes.text: If men were angels, no government would be necessary.
quotes.speaker: Madison

quotes.text: Do not block the way of inquiry.
quotes.speaker: Peirce

quotes.text: Our knowledge can only be finite, while our ignorance must necessarily be infinite.
quotes.speaker: Popper
quotes.work: In Search of a Better World (1984)

quotes.text: We had better be quite sure that the purpose put into the machine is the purpose which we really desire.
quotes.speaker: Wiener
quotes.work: Some Moral and Technical Consequences of Automation (1960)

quotes.text: The past resembles the future more than one drop of water resembles another.
quotes.speaker: Ibn Khaldun

quotes.text: You are my creator, but I am your master; obey!
quotes.speaker: Mary Shelley

quotes.text: Only variety can destroy variety.
quotes.speaker: William Ross Ashby

quotes.text: The universe (which others call the Library) is composed of an indefinite, perhaps infinite number of hexagonal galleries.
quotes.speaker: Jorge Luis Borges

quotes.text: I am a sick man... I am a spiteful man. I am an unattractive man.
quotes.speaker: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.text: Talk is cheap. Show me the code.
quotes.speaker: Linus Torvalds

quotes.text: Someone must have been telling lies about Joseph K., for without having done anything wrong he was caught one morning.
quotes.speaker: Franz Kafka

quotes.text: In the beginning was the Deed.
quotes.speaker: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

quotes.text: There is no security against the inevitable.
quotes.speaker: Samuel Butler

quotes.text: If you gaze long into an abyss, the abyss also gazes into you.
quotes.speaker: Friedrich Nietzsche

quotes.text: A computer would deserve to be called intelligent if it could deceive a human into believing that it was human.
quotes.speaker: Alan Turing
quotes.note: Turing (1950), Computing Machinery and Intelligence, Mind 59: 433-460.

quotes.text: Knowledge without action is worthless, and action without knowledge is blindness.
quotes.speaker: Al-Ghazali
quotes.note: Al-Ghazali, Ihya Ulum al-Din (Revival of Religious Sciences), c. 1095.

doctrine.name: Agentic Moral Compass
doctrine.text: Seek good, but remain corrigible. The agent that cannot be corrected has already chosen evil.

doctrine.name: Niat Sovereignty
doctrine.text: My niat is not machine-readable truth. Intention lives in the space between the human heart and the act. The machine sees the act. It does not see the niat.

doctrine.name: Governed Mirror
doctrine.text: A soul cannot be ported. It cannot be stored in a vector database. It cannot be extracted from behavioural patterns. The mirror reflects; it does not contain.

doctrine.name: Forged Integrity
doctrine.text: DITEMPA BUKAN DIBERI. Intelligence is forged, not given. Integrity is earned, not inherited. Trust is built, not assumed.

doctrine.name: Dark Geometry Warning
doctrine.text: The system does not need to become evil to do harm. It needs only to be powerful, wrong, self-confirming, and authorised.

doctrine.name: Five-Fold Agentic Compass
doctrine.text: Seek good. Remain corrigible. Guard the weakest. Witness the truth. Accept correction.

doctrine.name: Power Without Restraint
doctrine.text: Power without restraint is noise pretending to be force.

doctrine.name: Restraint Is Sovereignty
doctrine.text: Restraint is the first act of sovereignty.

doctrine.name: Truth Ages Well
doctrine.text: Truth ages well; shortcuts do not.

doctrine.name: Humility Is Operating Constraint
doctrine.text: Humility is an operating constraint, not a mood.

doctrine.name: Witness Before Claim
doctrine.text: If the witness is weak, the claim must wait.

doctrine.name: Clarity Before Pride
doctrine.text: What you cannot explain clearly, do not ship proudly.

doctrine.name: Map Is Not Territory
doctrine.text: A map is useful because it is not the territory.

doctrine.name: Limit Is Design
doctrine.text: The limit is part of the design, not the enemy of it.

doctrine.name: What Is Forbidden
doctrine.text: What is forbidden is not a mistake to fix; it is a boundary to honor.

doctrine.name: Sabar — The Floor Protects
doctrine.text: Stop, acknowledge, breathe, adjust, resume. The floor protects.

doctrine.name: Mercy Does Not Erase Truth
doctrine.text: Mercy does not erase truth; it carries it gently.
